newsitem.title: USA: NYC council tries to bar city use of Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: NYC council tries to bar city use of Swiss banks.

text.p: The New York City Council Speaker on Wednesday proposed a bill that would bar the city from depositing money in Swiss banks until the Swiss government established a compensation fund for Holocaust victims.
No estimate of how much money the city might have on deposit at such banks was immediately available, according to a spokeswoman for the Democrat-led City Council.

The bill was unveiled at City Hall by the Council Speaker, Peter Vallone. No response from Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, a Republican, was immediately available. If the mayor were to veto the bill, the council could overide it with a two-thirds vote, and Vallone in the past has been able to push tough votes through.
Saying it had been documented that Switzerland profited through trade with Nazi Germany, which paid for part of its war effort with gold stolen from conquered lands, the proposed bill said:

"Additionally, there is evidence of dormant accounts containing many millions of dollars in Swiss banks deposited by Jews who subsequently perished in the Holocaust. Until an acceptable compensation fund is established by the Swiss government for families of holocaust victims who were murdered by Nazis and had deposited such monies ie for safe-keeping, the City of New York does hereby set forth a municipal policy restricting its business with Swiss banks doing business in New York".
New York State's lawmakers also are weighing in on the issue, which was brought to the fore by U.S. Senator Al D'Amato, R-New York.

The New York State Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, plans to hold public hearings on Swiss banks and the unclaimed assets of Holocaust victims in New York City on February 13, according to a calender of hearings.
Assemblyman Brian McLaughlin, D-Queens, has drafted a bill that would amend the banking law to require an independent audit of accounts opened by Holocaust victims and protect dormant accounts.
